concerns.text: Tasks T010a and T010d instruct the implementer to 'hardcode' synthetic SMILES and rate constants, explicitly forbidding fetches from NIST/PubChem. This violates FR-008/FR-009 and Constitution Principle III (Data Hygiene) which mandate 'curated... derived from public literature' and 'real external data'. The task silently relaxes the requirement for real-world data sources to synthetic placeholders.

Task T023c implements a Wilcoxon signed-rank test as 'PRIMARY', explicitly overriding FR-006 which mandates a 'paired t-test'. Task T023d requires documenting this as a 'Plan Override'. This constitutes a scope violation where the task list unilaterally changes a functional requirement without a formal spec amendment or change request, violating the constraint preservation principle.

Task T016 mandates serialization to '.parquet' format, whereas the Plan.md (Project Structure) and implied data contracts for downstream model training (T019-T022) expect 'graphs.pt' (PyTorch Geometric format). This creates a data interface contradiction that breaks the deterministic flow required by the spec and plan.

Tasks T010g and T010h create a logical impossibility: T010g requires creating a schema with 'expected' hashes for files that do not yet exist (T010a/T010d), while T010h validates against this schema. This violates the constitutional requirement for reproducible data hygiene (Principle III) by attempting to pre-define checksums for synthetic data before generation, breaking the causal chain of data creation and verification.

Task T025 only archives model weights to a tarball. It fails to address FR-007 which requires logging 'all artifacts (model weights, attribution maps, metrics)' to the repository. The omission of attribution maps and metrics from the archival task violates the reproducibility constraint.
